content.value_statement: Azure authentication choices can be difficult to configure securely. This skill provides focused TypeScript examples for Azure Identity credentials, token providers, and cloud environments.
actual_capabilities: Select and configure DefaultAzureCredential for development and production.
Set up managed identities by system assignment, client ID, or resource ID.
Create service principal credentials using secrets or certificates.
Configure browser, device code, Azure CLI, Azure PowerShell, and Azure Developer CLI credentials.
Build custom credential chains and bearer token providers for Azure scopes.
Configure authority hosts for Azure Government and Azure China.
limitations: Provides guidance and examples but does not execute Azure authentication or verify tenant configuration.
Requires the Azure Identity package and valid identities, permissions, endpoints, and local developer tools.
Does not cover role assignment creation, tenant administration, certificate provisioning, or secret rotation.
Examples use placeholders and require environment-specific testing before production use.

use_cases.title: Authenticate an Azure SDK Client
use_cases.description: Add DefaultAzureCredential to a TypeScript service that accesses Azure Storage or another Azure SDK client.

use_cases.title: Replace Application Secrets
use_cases.description: Plan a migration from client secrets to managed identity for an Azure-hosted workload.

use_cases.title: Design a Credential Strategy
use_cases.description: Compare credential chains, sovereign cloud authorities, and developer login options for a multi-environment application.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up Default Credential
prompt_templates.prompt: Add Azure authentication to my TypeScript application using DefaultAzureCredential. Explain required packages, local prerequisites, and production behavior for [Azure service].
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for one Azure SDK client

prompt_templates.title: Configure Managed Identity
prompt_templates.prompt: Configure [system-assigned or user-assigned] managed identity for my TypeScript service running on [Azure host]. Include required identifiers and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Service Principal
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare client secret and certificate credentials for [application]. Recommend one based on deployment, rotation, and operational requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Advanced Credential Chain
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an Azure Identity strategy for [environments]. Include credential order, sovereign cloud support, failure handling, token scopes, and least-privilege controls.

output_examples.input: Which credential should a new Azure-hosted TypeScript service use?
output_examples.output: Use managed identity in Azure and DefaultAzureCredential in application code. It avoids stored production secrets and supports local developer credentials.

output_examples.input: How should I migrate from a client secret to managed identity?
output: Enable a system-assigned or user-assigned identity on the Azure host.
Grant only the required Azure role to that identity.
Replace ClientSecretCredential with DefaultAzureCredential or ManagedIdentityCredential.
Remove the old secret after deployment validation.

output_examples.output: Set the credential authority to AzureGovernment and use service endpoints for that cloud. Validate tenant access, scopes, and role assignments.

best_practices: Use DefaultAzureCredential when one code path must support local development and Azure hosting.
Prefer managed identity for production workloads to avoid storing client secrets.
Grant each identity only the Azure roles and scopes required by its workload.
anti_patterns: Do not commit tenant secrets, certificate passwords, access tokens, or private keys.
Do not use interactive browser or device code credentials for unattended production services.
Do not enable verbose authentication logging without reviewing logs for sensitive operational details.

faq.question: Which package does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses the official @azure/identity package and related Azure SDK credential interfaces.

faq.question: Does this skill execute Azure commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance and examples. You control package installation, code changes, authentication, and deployment.

faq.question: Which credential is recommended?
faq.answer: DefaultAzureCredential is the general starting point. ManagedIdentityCredential is useful when production behavior must be explicit.

faq.question: Can I use a service principal?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples cover client secrets and certificates, but production secrets still require secure storage and rotation.

faq.question: Does it support sovereign Azure clouds?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows authority host configuration for Azure Government and Azure China.

faq.question: Does it create role assignments?
faq.answer: No. Identity permissions and role assignments must be configured separately and validated against least-privilege requirements.
